_comment: Provenance for every compiled contract blueprint this backend ships: the CIP-113 core, the rwa-token substandard, and the four in-repo substandards.
The Aiken SOURCE for both used to be vendored into this repository (src/core-contracts
and src/substandards/rwa-token). It no longer is: the backend consumes only plutus.json,
and carrying ~1.2 MB of source to ship a 112 KB artifact duplicated files that upstream
already owns. What was worth keeping is this record -- WHICH upstream revision each
blueprint came from -- because without it the answer is only recoverable by scanning
upstream commits comparing validator hashes, which is exactly how this file came to exist.
The trade accepted with that removal: the blueprints can no longer be rebuilt or audited
from inside this repository. Both remain reproducible OUTSIDE it -- see docs/CONTRACTS.md
ContractBlueprintPinTest checks the sha256 values below on every build, so an accidental
edit to a blueprint fails loudly even though the source is gone.

blueprints.name: cip113-core
blueprints.note: Upstream's committed plutus.json, byte for byte, taken from the SDK's vendored copy at blueprints/standard/v0.5.0-alpha.5 and sha-verified against that directory's UPSTREAM_PIN.json. alpha.5 adds one check to protocol_params — the genesis mint must carry a withdraw-0 from the upgrade credential — which moves EIGHT of the twelve derived script hashes; always_fail, issuance_cbor_hex_mint, registry and upgrade_multisig survive because they hang off seeds and nonces. Pinned to the COMMIT, not the version string: upstream publishes no git tags, so 0.5.0-alpha.5 is a field inside a file on a moving branch.

blueprints.name: rwa-token
blueprints.note: NOT upstream's committed plutus.json. Upstream's is STALE: at this commit it does not reproduce from its own source -- global_state.global_state_spend_validator is committed as 57e2c6d5ca432b24871d113a1f0f4664ca4ea574d8ce892537356f49 (4901 bytes) where the source compiles to e720eb536b26eb8c639e96a17de4404ab4dbf18224ae9cc2242e13a9 (4698 bytes). plutus.json and validators/global_state.ak were last touched by the SAME commit, so the blueprint was committed without being regenerated after a final source edit. We ship the REBUILD, because the script that goes on chain must be the source that gets audited. Reproduce it by rebuilding upstream at this commit -- see docs/CONTRACTS.md. upstream_committed_sha256 records the stale bytes so it stays possible to tell whether upstream has since regenerated.

blueprints.name: dummy
blueprints.note: In-repo substandard: these bytes are the committed artifact of src/substandards/dummy/ at the pinned commit, byte for byte. `repository`/`commit` therefore name THIS repository rather than an upstream one -- the substandard's source lives here, so the revision that identifies the artifact is a commit of this repo. Rebuild with the pinned aiken_compiler; a different compiler yields different script hashes and a non-interoperable deployment.
